description: GitLab is the intelligent orchestration platform for DevSecOps. GitLab enables organizations to increase developer productivity, improve operational efficiency, reduce security and compliance risk, and accelerate digital transformation. More than 50 million registered users and more than 50% of the Fortune 100* trust GitLab to ship better, more secure software faster. The same principles built into our products are reflected in how our team works: we embrace AI as a core productivity multiplier, with all team members expected to incorporate AI into their daily workflows to drive efficiency, innovation, and impact. GitLab is where careers accelerate, innovation flourishes, and every voice is valued. Our high-performance culture is driven by our values and continuous knowledge exchange, enabling our team members to reach their full potential while collaborating with industry leaders to solve complex problems. Co-create the future with us as we build technology that transforms how the world develops software. Fortune 500® is a registered trademark of Fortune Media IP Limited, used under license. Claim based on GitLab data. Fortune 100 refers to the top 20% ranked companies in the 2025 Fortune 500 list, published in June 2025. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab. An overview of this role As a Software Engineer on GitLab's Authorization team, you'll help build and maintain the system that decides what every user, token, and automated agent can access on GitLab.com, Self-Managed, and Dedicated. You'll work alongside experienced engineers who guide the larger design decisions, delivering well-scoped changes and growing into ownership of larger parts of the system. Today, that work is Ruby on Rails. Roughly 400 policy classes and a catalog of about 1,900 permissions sit behind every application programming interface (API) request. You'll work on fine-grained token permissions, custom roles, and the GraphQL and representational state transfer (REST) APIs that enforce them. A single request can trigger hundreds of permission checks, so correctness and performance both matter. You'll also contribute to moving the permission model to a new authorization stack that pairs the Rails monolith with a Rust policy engine. The engine represents access relationships and evaluates permission rules, and can run within the monolith's process or be reached through remote procedure calls using gRPC. You don't need prior Rust experience: several engineers on the team learned it for this work, and we'll support you doing the same. Some examples of our projects: Refactoring GitLab's policy layer so the same permission definitions can be evaluated by the monolith and the new authorization service Extending fine-grained token permissions to more resources, with guidance from senior engineers on the design What you'll do Implement authorization changes in GitLab's Ruby on Rails monolith so permission checks allow intended access and deny unauthorized access. Deliver well-scoped workstreams from feature-flagged rollout through verifying that the old and new systems produce the same results, with review and guidance from senior engineers. Build and extend fine-grained permissions for tokens and roles so additional resources have permission coverage consistent with the established catalog. Extend and fix authorization enforcement so GraphQL and the REST API enforce the intended permissions consistently. Make incremental refactors to long-lived policy code without changing behavior for existing customers. Investigate and fix reliability, performance, and security issues so affected permission checks return the expected results without regressions. Work with the authentication, platform, and artificial intelligence (AI) teams to document interface contracts that keep permission checks consistent as authorization moves toward a shared service. Contribute to design documents, merge requests, and code reviews so proposed changes have a documented rationale and review feedback is addressed asynchronously. What you'll bring Solid experience building and maintaining production Ruby on Rails applications, typically gained over 2 to 4 years or more. Hands-on experience with authorization concepts, such as role-based access control or fine-grained permissions, from work or projects. A security mindset: you treat a permission bug as a security bug and consider who a change could affect before choosing an implementation. Experience making careful changes to existing codebases, including incremental refactors and feature-flagged rollouts that preserve existing behavior. Familiarity with GraphQL or API authorization patterns. Awareness of performance, including how repeated permission checks can add up on every request. Strong written communication and the ability to work effectively when most decisions happen in a document or merge request rather than a meeting. Helpful, but not required: hands-on PostgreSQL experience, or experience with Rust, gRPC or Protocol Buffers, Cedar or other policy languages, Zanzibar-style authorization systems, Go, or service-oriented architecture. We welcome transferable experience from adjacent domains such as identity, policy engines, and platform security. About the team We work in a fully asynchronous organization, with most decisions made in documents or merge requests rather than meetings. Our values include collaboration, results, efficiency, diversity, inclusion and belonging, iteration, and transparency. We expect all GitLab team members to incorporate AI into their daily workflows to drive efficiency, innovation, and impact. We are seeking a Staff QA Engineer to join our Broadband and Network group Location-Bangalore (Hybrid) In this role, you will be responsible for validating and testing cloud-native microservices that seamlessly integrate with complex embedded systems. The position requires strong expertise in distributed architectures, CMTS /DOCIS domain ,hands-on troubleshooting skills, and the ability to develop, execute, and enhance automated test frameworks across both microservices and embedded platforms. The ideal candidate will be capable of identifying and resolving issues across the full technology stack, ensuring scalability, reliability, and high-quality software delivery. How You’ll help us connect the world: Define test strategies/test plans, and validation approaches for cloud-native microservices, CMTS/DOCSIS platforms, and embedded devices Create and maintain detailed test cases covering functional, integration, system, resiliency, scalability, performance, and end-to-end workflows. Execute end-to-end, integration, regression, interoperability, and system-level test suites. Investigate and troubleshoot complex issues across distributed microservices, CMTS/DOCSIS components, embedded systems, and networking infrastructure. Analyze logs, traces, telemetry data, packet captures, and system metrics to isolate root causes. Work in scrum model and collaborate closely with R&D Scrum teams to investigate complex issues, providing detailed technical analysis and reproducible scenarios Provide on-demand SQA customer support for issue triage, verification, and release confidence Utilize Automations and Debugging tool clubbed AI technology to improve test coverage, execution efficiency, and root-cause analysis build, configure, and maintain complex test labs consisting of CMTS platforms, DOCSIS devices, embedded systems, virtualized environments, and cloud-native services. Manage hardware, network topology, simulators, traffic generators, and test environments required for large-scale validation Work with developers, product management, DevOps, and customer support teams to address critical issues and improve product quality. Design and develop scalable automation frameworks using Java, Python, or Go. Required Qualifications: Bachelor’s degree in computer science or equivalent with 8+ years in QA, or software engineering testing of an Embedded System (HW/SW) with Microservices. Exposure to AI-assisted test automation and quality engineering practices. Experience in QA methodologies, Scripting experience (Python, Bash, etc.) Linux knowledge, Strong experience in CMTS/DOCSIS technologies and broadband networking domains . Deep understanding of cloud-native microservices architectures , APIs, containers, and distributed systems Strong debugging and troubleshooting skills involving logs, packet captures, telemetry, and system diagnostics. Experience with DHCP, DNS, NAT, IPv4/IPv6 Hands-on with Wireshark, tcpdump, Iperf / traffic generators such as Ixia, Spirent You will Excite us if you have: Knowledge of CTMS architectures and traffic engineering concepts. Experience with Kafka, Redis, Elasticsearch, Prometheus, Grafana, and Splunk. fundamental networking protocols: IPv4/IPv6 routing, switching, Multicast, IGMP, DHCP, and TOD.-good to have Why Join Us? Our global team of innovators and employees are trusted advisors who listen to customers first, then deliver value. description: AVEVA is creating software trusted by over 90% of leading industrial companies.
